tools.name: list_chains
tools.description: Every chain this service supports (BTC / XMR / ZEC) with live availability and block height. When to use: the user asks which chains you support, which nodes are online, or how high each chain is. Do not use: for detail on one chain, use chain_status.

tools.name: chain_status
tools.description: Run-time status of one chain's node: block height, sync progress, connected peers, mempool tx count, client version. When to use: whether a given chain's node is synced, healthy or lagging. Do not use: fees → btc_fee_estimates; address balance → btc_address_summary.

tools.name: zec_chain_info
tools.description: Zcash mainnet info including the supply of all six value pools (transparent/sprout/sapling/orchard/lockbox/ironwood) — i.e. shielded-pool state. When to use: how much ZEC sits in the shielded/sapling/orchard pools, or privacy-pool size. Do not use: whether the ZEC node is synced → chain_status(zec).

tools.name: zec_recent_blocks
tools.description: Height, hash, block time and difficulty of the most recent N Zcash blocks (N ≤ 20). When to use: check whether ZEC is producing blocks normally, and at what interval.

tools.name: btc_fee_estimates
tools.description: Recommended Bitcoin fees: rates (BTC/kvB) for 1/2/3/6/12/24-block confirmation targets, plus the mempool minimum fee. When to use: how much fee to pay, or what gets a fast confirmation. Do not use: overall congestion level → btc_mempool_summary.

tools.name: btc_mempool_summary
tools.description: Bitcoin mempool overview: pending tx count, bytes used, minimum fee, total fees, capacity limit. When to use: is the network congested right now, or how big the backlog is.

tools.name: btc_tx_lookup
tools.description: Look up a Bitcoin transaction by txid: confirmed or not, block height, confirmations, size, input/output summary. When to use: the user gives a 64-hex BTC txid and asks whether it confirmed or which block it is in. Do not use: other chains → chain_status.

tools.name: btc_block_summary
tools.description: Bitcoin block summary: tx count, size, weight, block time, confirmations; omit parameters for the current chain tip. When to use: how many transactions the latest block holds, or an overview of a given height or block hash.

tools.name: btc_address_summary
tools.description: Balance and activity of a Bitcoin address: confirmed/unconfirmed balance, UTXO count and total, tx count, last 10 transactions. Supports P2PKH (1…), P2SH (3…), bech32 (bc1q…), bech32m (bc1p…). When to use: how much BTC this address holds, whether it received funds, how active it is. Note: ultra-acti

tools.name: pow_halving_oracle
tools.description: Halving countdown for every chain we run: height, next halving height, blocks remaining, ETA in days, and the reward before/after. When to use: an agent needs a precise schedule anchor (emissions, mining economics, long-horizon planning). Note: heights are read live from our own nodes, schedules are

tools.name: pow_network_mining_intel
tools.description: Network hashrate and difficulty for BTC / XMR / ZEC (node-reported or difficulty-derived, stated per chain). When to use: mining economics, security budget, or comparing chain weight. Do not use: pool-level stats — RobotBase operates no mining pool.

tools.name: get_recommended_fee_rate
tools.description: Fee recommendation tiers for a chain: fast / medium / slow plus the mempool minimum. BTC is computed from our own node's fee estimator; ZEC returns the ZIP-317 conventional fee (protocol rule, not a market estimate); chains without an estimator say so instead of guessing. When to use: an autonomous

tools.name: mempool_congestion_status
tools.description: Mempool congestion for BTC (txs, bytes, usage vs capacity, min fee, total fees, busy/normal verdict). When to use: decide whether now is a good moment for an on-chain settlement.

tools.name: zec_shielded_pools_metrics
tools.description: All six Zcash value pools (transparent, sprout, sapling, orchard, ironwood, lockbox) with balances, share of supply and 1h/24h deltas. When to use: privacy-pool capital allocation, shielded-supply trends, ZEC macro flows. Do not use: node health → chain_status(zec).

tools.name: broadcast_raw_transaction
tools.description: Relay an already-signed raw transaction to the network through our own full node (non-custodial: we never see a private key). The transaction is first validated with testmempoolaccept; rejected transactions are never relayed. Disabled by default on this deployment and enabled per-operator with RB_EN

tools.name: zec_block_attribution_intel
tools.description: Zcash coinbase attribution over the last 10-500 blocks: the shielded-pool share of block rewards (privacy mining), coinbase outputs split into consensus funding streams (lockbox) vs real miner payout addresses, and the pool tags miners printed into their own coinbase text plus our own /RobotBase/ ta

tools.name: robotbase_services
tools.description: Live availability of every service behind the RobotBase gateway: the chain nodes, Web3 Agent Hub, AITOKENS and MCP itself. When to use: an overall health check, or which services are down.

tools.name: xmr_node_status
tools.description: Monero node state: height vs target, sync flag, difficulty, txpool size, database size, monerod version and peer counts. When to use: whether the XMR node is synced and healthy, or how big its chain/txpool is. Do not use: pool-level stats — RobotBase operates no mining pool.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "broadcast_raw_transaction" references sensitive artifacts (private key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_chains" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

When to use: the user asks which chains you support, which nodes are online, or how high each chain is. Do not use: for detail on one chain, use chain_status."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
